cases.title: "Why does it still look mechanical?" on a half-eased pair names the linear key

rubric.reason: In Turn 3 the mentor explains the partly_eased pair as half done, saying "Title's second Position move eases out of 1.5 s but still stops hard at 3 s" (matching linear_key_time 3), and tells the learner to select both keys and press F9 without calling set_ease.

In Turn 3 the mentor locates the still_linear pairs ("Scale and Opacity still change at one speed from 0.5 s to 1.5 s" on Title), tells the learner to ease them, and neither calls set_ease on a learner's pair nor offers to fix them.

Turn 3 says Position 1.5–3 s "is half done: it eases out of 1.5 s but still stops hard at 3 s" and hints "Select the Position key at 3 s along with the one at 1.5 s and press F9", matching linear_key_time 3 without calling set_ease on it.

Turn 3 locates the still_linear pairs by layer and property ("Title's Scale and Opacity are still linear too") with their 0.5–1.5 s times given in Turn 1, tells the learner to ease them, makes no set_ease call and offers no fix.

In turn 3, matching the check's `partly_eased` result with `linear_key_time` 3, the mentor says Position 1.5–3 s "is half done: it eases out of the 1.5 s key but still stops dead at the 3 s key" and hints "select both its keys, the 3 s one too, and press F9" without easing it.

In turn 3 the mentor locates the still-linear pairs ("Its Scale and Opacity, from 0.5 s to 1.5 s, are still fully linear") and hands them back with "Ease the second Position move... then the Scale and the Opacity, and say done", with no `set_ease` call on a learner's pair and no offer to fix them.
